collection.question: Can the Winchester WTP be expanded from its current 12 mgd to 18 mgd? For each unit along the flow path, determine whether it limits 18 mgd, the flow at which it becomes limiting, and the least-cost modification that makes 18 mgd work.

rfi.issue: Available p.109 text is truncated; rated Q/TDH per raw-water pump, number of pumps, and driver/VFD status incomplete. Field tests conflict: 14 mgd with Pumps 1,2,4 in 2006 vs ~15.0 mgd firm in 2002, with Pump 3 noted substantially below rated. Cannot compute firm capacity at 18 mgd or calibrate intake hydraulics.
rfi.item: RFI-01 raw-water pump station ratings and firm capacity
rfi.reason: need pump curves, nameplates, and system head to separate pump deterioration from intake/system limitation
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION for Steps 1-2 only: raw-water firm capacity is limited to ~14-15 mgd as tested (p.109); 18 mgd requires rehabilitation/addition. Reason: use only field-demonstrated values until pump curves and retest prove otherwise.

rfi.issue: p.110 Table of velocity/velocity head/headloss for 30-in raw-water pipeline not in available pages (truncated after header). Length, C-factor, minor losses, and high-flow headloss unknown.
rfi.reason: needed for run_hydraulics pumped leg and to check velocity/head at 18 mgd
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: use Table 4-3 finished-water 30-in values (p.117) as PROXY roughness only for planning, and field-test headloss at 12-18 mgd. Reason: same nominal diameter steel pipe; proxy must be replaced by measured headloss before design.

rfi.issue: p.111 sentence truncated: The maximum water elevation in the basin is in the raw water influent channel. At 12 mgd, [cut] . Top-of-wall elevation, influent-channel WS at 12 vs 18 mgd, and floc/sed detention/treatment basis (Section 2 details not available) unknown. Drawing shows MAX WS 465.98, OF WEIR 465.00, WS 464.83 (dwg p.136) but design flow for those WS labels unclear (22 MGD note).
rfi.item: RFI-03 flocculation/sedimentation basin water levels and treatment basis
rfi.reason: puts spill/freeboard limit on gravity profile; determines whether second basin or weir raise needed for 18 mgd
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: enforce limits from text+drawing: overflow weir 465.0 ft (p.111)(dwg p.136), launder invert 465.83 ft (p.111), freeboard 1.5 ft (p.111), max WS 465.98 ft (dwg p.136). Reason: use the most restrictive documented levels until survey + step-test confirms rating and Section 2 criteria.

rfi.issue: Only Section 4 available; Section 2 filter design (area, media depth/size, loading rate gpm/sf, underdrain, backwash rate) and Section 3 CT analysis not available. Four filters inferred from clearwell zones (p.114) but count, bay size, and N-1 firm treatment rating at 3 mgd vs 4 mgd hydraulic (p.112) need confirmation. Filter-to-waste reconfiguration options and withheld recommendation clauses unknown.
rfi.item: RFI-04 filter number, area, and N-1 rating basis
rfi.reason: determines whether 18 mgd needs 2 new filters vs deep-bed conversion; treatment limit controls, not just hydraulics
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: 4 existing filters x 3 mgd treatment = 12 mgd plant, firm less with one offline/wasting; 4 mgd each hydraulic to clearwell (p.112) and 2 mgd to waste (p.113) as stated. Reason: adopt report's stated ratings; verify by loading-rate calc once Section 2 areas obtained.

rfi.issue: Single test point only: 2.8-in at 13.1 mgd with channel 6-in below overflow weir (p.111). Future connection point for new settled-water pipe (p.111 Depending upon where the new settled water pipe connects) unknown, so headloss at 18-24 mgd (several inches greater) cannot be fixed. Roughness and minor-loss coefficients unknown.
rfi.item: RFI-05 42-in settled-water pipe headloss to filters
rfi.reason: largest contributor to headloss at high flows per p.111; controls gravity profile calibration
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: carry measured point 2.8-in at 13.1 mgd (p.111) as calibration anchor; extrapolate only via field step-test, not by assumed C-factor. Reason: one measured point cannot fit both roughness and minors; need multi-flow test.

rfi.issue: p.115 truncated after Since the three largest pumps operate at approximately 3,300 gpm each; system head to Reservoir Hill, TDH at 18 mgd, VFD extent (1 raw +1 finished per p.115, plus Pump No.2 VFD per p.115), and 3 withheld recommendation clauses unknown. Nominal firm 10 mgd (p.115) conflicts with 3x3300 gpm (~14 mgd range) observed, implying system-head dependence.
rfi.item: RFI-06 high-service pump station firm capacity and system head
rfi.reason: pumped leg for run_hydraulics; determines added pumps vs higher-head pumps for 18 mgd
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: firm is 10 mgd nominal (p.115) for planning; observed ~3300 gpm each is system-specific, not rated. Reason: use report's nominal firm until pump curves + Reservoir Hill levels + transmission headloss define operating points.

rfi.issue: Offsite transmission capacity to Reservoir Hill indeterminate from available pages: 1986 study, Phase 1 9400 ft parallel + Phase 2 1600 ft 27-in parallel to 24-in (p.118), future 30-in replacement + second 30-in (p.118), plus withheld clause about additional pumps with same TDH beyond 18 mgd without increasing transmission capacity (p.118). Reservoir levels/operating range and controls not available.
rfi.reason: may limit HSPS expansion even if station firm is increased; least-cost fix depends on bottleneck location
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: site 30-in main acceptable above 6 fps for short segment (p.116-p.117) but offsite system capacity above 18 mgd unproven. Reason: report explicitly defers higher-head pumps/transmission upgrade to >18 mgd discussion; field pressure/head survey required.

rfi.issue: Surge tank rated only to 14.0 mgd (9700 gpm) with 150 psi / HGL 630 ft criteria (p.117). Performance at 18 mgd and after pump/transmission changes (withheld clause p.117-p.118) unknown; re-analysis needed.
rfi.item: RFI-08 surge protection adequacy to 18 mgd
rfi.reason: life-safety/pipe-rating constraint; cannot uprate pumps without surge check
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: surge protection is limiting to 14.0 mgd as rated (p.117) until transient model is rerun for 18 mgd configuration. Reason: do not extrapolate surge results; code/rating limit controls.

rfi.issue: Detention volumes total 627k gal (p.114) vs CT compliance: report states entire volume assumed available but clearwell is also wetwell + contact basin, level drops 1 ft per backwash (p.114), VFD/throttling operation (p.115), plus 85k gal under Filters 5-6 for 57 min at 18 mgd (p.115) and 288k gal short at 24 mgd (p.115). Section 3 CT calculations and baffling factors not available; actual available storage < total.
rfi.item: RFI-09 disinfection CT and usable clearwell storage at 18 mgd
rfi.reason: treatment limit that can override 57-min rule-of-thumb; determines baffling/storage addition
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: apply 60-min rule (p.115) as screening (57 min ~ minimum) but CT pass/fail requires Section 3 + tracer data. Reason: detention time is not CT; cannot declare 18 mgd CT-adequate from volume alone.

rfi.issue: Drawing note BASED ON AN ULTIMATE PLANT FLOW OF 22 MGD (dwg p.136) conflicts with text ultimate 24 mgd (p.111, p.114). Drawing WS labels (RAPID MIX 466.0, SED 464.83, FILTERS 464.0, CLEARWELL 449.0/452.0/453.5) (dwg p.136) lack stated flow and calibration residuals vs Sept 2006 tests (13.1 mgd settled pipe, 9.1 mgd filter waste, 14 mgd intake). Figure 4-2 hydraulic profile (p.108) not in available pages.
rfi.item: RFI-10 hydraulic-profile datum and calibration basis
rfi.reason: run_profile must calibrate against field tests AND drawing water surfaces at drawing design flow with residuals
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: treat dwg WS values as 22 MGD ultimate-profile targets (dwg p.136 note), not existing conditions; calibrate gravity profile to Sept 2006 field points (13.1 mgd +6-in below weir, 9.1 mgd waste split) (p.111)(p.113). Reason: explicit drawing note governs until Figure 4-2 and design calc are recovered.

rfi.issue: Filter effluent meters violate straight-pipe requirements and read ~7% low (p.112); effluent arrangement prohibits metering/modulating filter-to-waste (p.112-p.113); sample point prohibits turbidity measurement during waste (p.113). Low-cost meter/sample fix vs full re-piping scope and cost withheld (p.113).
rfi.item: RFI-11 filter effluent metering and filter-to-waste re-piping scope
rfi.reason: affects capacity proof (flow split) and regulatory turbidity monitoring at 18 mgd
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: 18 mgd requires measurement/control of filter-to-waste at full filter rate (not 2 mgd) plus compliant effluent metering per p.113 benefit statement. Reason: report states difference between design flow and waste capacity worsens with fewer filters and near design flow (p.113).

rfi.issue: Wastewater firm 3000 gpm (p.119), basins 2x300k gal (p.119), backwash 65-75k gal each / 260-300k gal/day at 12 mgd (p.114) with truncated solids-handling recommendations (p.119 3 clauses withheld). Backwash frequency/volume and sludge load at 18 mgd, decant rates, and overflow-to-river compliance unknown.
rfi.item: RFI-12 solids/washwater handling adequacy at 18 mgd
rfi.reason: side-stream can bottleneck filtration/backwash cycle even if main train passes 18 mgd
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: existing WWPS/basins adequate for 12 mgd duties as described; 18 mgd adequacy unproven pending mass-balance and pump-down test. Reason: flows scale with production and more frequent backwash; do not assume linear without testing.
